newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian bullion down on poor world trends.
newsitem.headline: Indian bullion down on poor world trends.

text.p: Gold 24 carat closed 5 rupees lower at 4,450 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,455 rupees but up 20 rupees against the opening level of 4,430 rupees, dealer said.
"Gold prices opened lower on higher supplies and losses in the world market but later on renewed physical buying trimmed early losses towards the close," they said.
Meanwhile prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) closed 100 rupees lower at 52,000 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees on Monday. They were up by 1,400 rupees per piece during last week.
"Renewed physical buying ahead of the Hindu festival season dragged gold upward towards the close after easy start," on broker said.

Silver (.999) closed 45 rupees lower at 6,275 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,320 rupees but up 10 rupees against the opening level of 6,265 rupees as fresh industrial buying helped prices to bounce back after lower start.

In early trade silver was weak on higher supplies and setback in the world market but later on industrial buying dragged prices upward towards the close. Silver was down by 50 rupees per kg on Monday and by 90 rupees during last week.
The Bombay bullion market will remain officially closed on Wednesday to mark a Hindu festival. The market will reopen for trade on Thursday.
